info.bio: Klaus Nomi, nacido como Klaus Sperber (Immenstadt im Allgäu, 24 de enero, 1944 – Nueva York, 6 de agosto, 1983) fue un contratenor de origen alemán, ampliamente reconocido por sus excepcionales interpretaciones vocales y por fusionar la ópera con el rock y el pop. Nomi es recordado por sus extravagantes actuaciones teatrales, su maquillaje recargado, su vestuario futurista, y su peinado estilizado que exageraba las entradas de su cabello. scenes.name: Club 57, Mudd Club y el arte del downtown
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Dos clubes rivales como laboratorios artísticos. El Club 57, en el sótano de una iglesia polaca, era «groovy»: fiestas temáticas de Ann Magnuson, Kenny Scharf, Keith Haring y John Sex, camp, travestismo y psicodelia, con Klaus Nomi y la anti-banda Pulsallama. El Mudd Club de Steve Maas era «cool»: decadencia no wave, metacualona y heroína, el «Funeral del rock'n'roll» y la fiesta del soul de Michael Holman. Allí tocaba Gray, el grupo de ruido de Jean-Michel Basquiat, Holman y Vincent Gallo; Basquiat produjo «Beat Bop» de Rammellzee y el downtown abrazó el grafiti y el hip hop. El boom de las galerías (FUN, Times Square Show, New York/New Wave), la llegada de Reagan, la «Operation Pressure Point» de Giuliani y el sida acabaron con el diletantismo: «era cuestión de crear o morir».

podcast.body: Klaus Nomi tragically died of AIDS-related complications, making him one of the earliest celebrities to succumb to the disease. "Nomi died of AIDS-related complications, making him one of the first celebrities to die of the disease."

podcast.title: Collaboration with David Bowie
podcast.body: David Bowie, after seeing Klaus Nomi perform live, was so impressed that he invited Nomi to collaborate. This led to Nomi's appearance with Bowie on Saturday Night Live on December 15, 1979, where he provided backup vocals on three songs. "And that led to Nomi's appearance with Bowie on Saturday Night Live. The date was December 15, 1979. He sang back up on three songs."

podcast.title: Death from AIDS-Related Complications
podcast.body: Klaus Nomi died from AIDS-related complications, making him one of the first celebrities whose death was attributed to the disease. His music is currently difficult to find in physical copies, though it remains available on platforms like YouTube. "Nomi died of AIDS-related complications, making him one of the first celebrities to die of the disease."

podcast.title: Deeter's Monkey Namesake
podcast.body: The avant-garde singer Klaus Nomi lent his name to Klaus, the monkey character featured in Mike Myers' "Sprockets" sketch on Saturday Night Live. This detail highlights Nomi's distinct presence in avant-garde music, influencing pop culture references. "And Deeter's monkey, Klaus, was named after the avant-garde singer, Klaus Nomi."

podcast.title: Early Life and Artistic Development
podcast.body: Originally German, Klaus Nomi developed a love for opera and began singing it in a gay disco in West Berlin before relocating to New York. His performances evolved to become increasingly otherworldly, incorporating wild costumes, makeup, hair, and elaborate stage effects like smoke, strobes, and explosions, blending opera, vaudeville, technopop, and new wave. "Clouse was German, and he loved opera. He even sang opera in a gay disco in West Berlin before moving to New York."

podcast.body: Klaus Nomi, a German artist, had a strong affinity for opera and began his career singing opera in a gay disco in West Berlin. After moving to New York, his performances grew increasingly otherworldly, incorporating wild costumes, makeup, and elaborate hair. His live shows were known for dramatic elements like smoke, strobes, and explosions. "Clouse was German, and he loved opera. He even sang opera in a gay disco in West Berlin before moving to New York, and the more he performed, the more otherworldly he became, wild costumes and makeup and hair."

podcast.title: New York Underground Recognition
podcast.body: Nomi became a prominent figure in the New York Underground scene, gaining recognition and being embraced by influential artists such as Keith Haring and Jean-Michel Basquiat. "He became a fixture in the New York Underground scene, and was embraced by artists such as Keith Herring and John Michel Basquit."

podcast.title: New York Underground and David Bowie Collaboration
podcast.body: Nomi became a prominent figure in the New York Underground scene, gaining recognition from artists such as Keith Haring and Jean-Michel Basquiat. David Bowie, upon hearing about Nomi, rushed to see one of his live shows. This led to Nomi's appearance with Bowie on Saturday Night Live on December 15, 1979, where Nomi sang backup on three songs. "He became a fixture in the New York Underground scene and was embraced by artists such as Keith Haring and Johnny Shell Basquit."

xref.title: Deeter Character Inspiration
xref.body: Mike Myers was inspired to create the character Deeter from the "Sprockets" sketch on Saturday Night Live by observing a waiter at a venue called the Camerunhouse in Toronto. The sketch also featured a Kraftwerk song played at the wrong speed as its theme, and Deeter's monkey, Klaus, was named after avant-garde singer Klaus Nomi. "Lord has it that Mike Myers was inspired to create Deeter by a waiter at a venue called the Camerunhouse in Toronto."
